text: You already know how to read the navigator as a user, from Course 2. Lesson 25 had you build one module without fully explaining what holds it in place. This lesson opens up the two real record types that define your own application's section of that tree.

When you create a scoped application, the platform automatically creates an Application Menu record, carrying the application's own name — that's the top-level entry a user expands in the navigator. Every module nested underneath it sets its Application menu field to point back at that one record. Skip that field, and a module floats loose instead of nesting where it belongs. Set Order on each module, and lower numbers simply appear higher among their siblings.

The Link type field isn't cosmetic — it changes what actually happens on click. List of Records, the type Lesson 25 used, opens a table's list view, optionally pre-filtered. Record opens one specific record directly, the right fit for a single settings or configuration record rather than a list of many. URL opens a fixed or argument-built address, internal or external, with no table-backed screen needed at all. UI Page opens a custom-rendered screen, built the way Chapter 4 covered, reached as a module exactly like any list view would be.

Two more fields matter on any module. Order, a plain number, controls position among sibling modules under the same menu — your most-used module gets the lowest number. Role, if set, controls visibility instead of position: only users holding that role even see the module in the navigator, with no error and no visible gap for everyone else. That's a separate concern from Chapter 5's application scope, which controls what code outside the app can call, not what a logged-in user sees in their own tree.

An Application Menu holding the tree together, modules nested inside it with the right link type, Order, and Role — that's the whole mechanism behind a usable custom application. Lesson 27 puts all of it to work in one complete worked scenario, from table design to a navigable app.
